name: MOP (Muriate of Potash)
source: RESOLVED (2026-09-27), third check: PIB Release ID 2237470, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, 10 Mar 2026 ('Government Stabilizes Fertilizer Prices for Rabi 2025-26'), Smt. Anupriya Patel (MoS) in a written reply to a Rajya Sabha Unstarred Question -- states directly: 'The average retail prices for other key grades (per 50 kg bag) for the 2025-26 period are: ... Muriate of Potash (MOP): Rs.1710.54' -> 34.2108/kg, rounded to 34.21. This is a government-reported market-average retail price (across manufacturers, for the current Rabi 2025-26 season), not one company's own MRP list the way urea/DAP/28-28/10-26-26 are (IFFCO's) -- flagged as a different kind of source, still a real, dated, primary citation, not invented. Two earlier passes had checked IFFCO's own price list (doesn't carry MOP) and general market listings (too inconsistent, Rs.9-1500/kg-equivalent) without success; found on a third, more targeted pass searching specifically for a Rabi-2025-26-period PIB release, the same category of source already used for the NBS subsidy figures below. Standard grade 0-0-60 per Indian Potash Ltd / industry convention; bag_size_kg=50 explicitly stated in this same source ('per 50 kg bag'). Government SUBSIDY on MOP (separate from this retail price) is Rs.1428/MT per PIB Release ID 2211384, 5 Jan 2026 -- not used as price_inr_per_kg, since that's paid to companies, not the farmer-facing price.
